records.source_name: IEC 60050 — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary
records.version_or_edition: current
records.notes: Used as governance anchor for electronics and electrical engineering terminology. IEC 60050 serves as the primary reference set for scientific and engineering vocabulary in this domain. Signal categories supported: electromagnetic principles (voltage, current, frequency), semiconductor devices (transistor), sensing phenomena (piezoelectric, Hall effect, infrared, ultrasonic, capacitive), communication protocols (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT), and action verbs denoting electronic behavior (detects, measures, converts, transmits). Individual signals are compiled from this baseline; not every term is directly defined in IEC 60050 but all are consistent with its vocabulary scope.

records.notes: Source for the Electrical / Electronics Technical Deepening Slice 1 reference claims ohms_law_reference and electrical_power_vi_reference (reference_fundamentals group basic_electrical_reference_v1): Ohm's law as written in the handbook, E = I × R / E = IR (handbook page 14), where the source identifies E = voltage (V), I = current (A) and R = resistance (Ω); and electric power, P = I × E / P = IE (handbook page 16). The handbook uses E for voltage; InventorAI presents the SAME relationships as V = I × R (V = IR) and P = V × I (P = VI) because the product and SI unit presentation use V for voltage — a notation normalization only; it is not claimed that DOE wrote V = I × R or P = V × I. The official PDF was available on the DOE surface at inspection; no URL is recorded in this entry. Source-use disposition: electronics_electrical:PR006. Bounded reference relationships only — no project-specific calculation and no applicability inference.
